Department of Interior June 28, 1972
Page Three
I. Adequate Differentiation Between Classes
of ORRVs and ORRV Uses -
We are surprised and disappointed to note that neither the Draft Statement (and the proposed regulations discussed therein) nor the Task Force Study's recommendations make any reference to any intention to give consideration to varying types of ORRVs and ORRV uses in establishing the final regulations under the Executive Order. We fail to see how any regulatory program can properly balance the need for minimization of adverse environmental impact against the need to promote recreational use without carefully classifying the possible impacts of the varying types of ORRV use and tailoring the regulatory approach to take into account the specific requirements of each type of vehicle.*
This failure to differentiate between ORRV classifications would be especially discriminatory and unjustified in respect to its impact on opportunities for snowmobile use since the snowmobile's impact on the environment, as compared to that of other ORRV types, is insignificant.
Snowmobile operation takes place in the winter when the land is dormant and well covered by a protective blanket of snow and the snowmobile is designed to be supported on wide skis and a flexible track of sufficient width to provide flotation on the snow.
